diagnostic_evidence.quote: The analysis in this section assumes the electric field $E^{n+1}$ is given and fixed during the kinetic update. In the full VPFP system, $E$ is coupled to $\rho$ via the Poisson equation. A complete AP analysis of the fully nonlinear coupled system would require accounting for errors in the macroscopic field solver, which is beyond the scope of this work.
This macroscopic drift system represents the high-field limit of the VPFP system as $\varepsilon \to 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The advertised AP claim requires showing that, for fixed discretization parameters as $\varepsilon\to0$, the coupled numerical scheme reduces to a consistent discretization of the macroscopic drift system. The formal result only bounds the collision residual and distance to a Maxwellian for a fixed supplied field, with an assumed bounded residual and an additional $\mathcal O(\kappa_h)$ term. The source expressly states that the density–Poisson coupling needed for a complete AP analysis is not treated.

failure_location.quote: For the first-order scheme, we prove an asymptotic-preserving (AP) property when the field fluctuation is small.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either prove convergence of the coupled density and Poisson updates to a consistent discretization of the macroscopic drift system or withdraw the AP guarantee and describe the result as a fixed-field relaxation estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The paper does not establish its advertised AP guarantee for the fully coupled first-order VPFP scheme; it establishes only a conditional kinetic relaxation estimate.
issues.title: Relaxation estimate is presented as a full asymptotic-preserving result
issues.why_classification: The source supplies no complete coupled AP argument, and the available repair either requires new global analysis or removes a central advertised guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: However, applying the IMEX scheme  \eqref{eq:full_tensor_imex} across all K-S-L steps leads to instability, because the S-step evolves backward in time.

As suggested in \cite{zhang2025stability}, we propose a hybrid IMEX scheme: the K and L steps use an implicit (backward Euler) update for the Fokker--Planck operator, while the S step uses an explicit (forward Euler) update.

issues.failure_explanation: The second-order scheme nevertheless treats the collision operator implicitly in each backward S-stage. On a projected collision mode with eigenvalue $-\lambda$ for $\lambda>0$, the displayed stage reduces, with advection suppressed, to $(1-(\Delta t/4)\lambda/\varepsilon)S^*=S$. It is singular when $(\Delta t/4)\lambda/\varepsilon=1$ and arbitrarily ill-conditioned nearby. Thus the procedure is not well defined or uniformly stable over the claimed stiff parameter regime, precisely the failure that motivated explicit treatment of the first-order S-step.

failure_location.quote: \State \textbf{S-step} ($\Delta t/2$): Evolve $S$ to obtain $S^{(2)}$ via 2nd-order IMEX.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, the S-substeps must be replaced by a second-order treatment that remains well defined and stable uniformly in $\Delta t/\varepsilon$, followed by a renewed accuracy and stability analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The proposed second-order algorithm lacks a well-defined, uniformly robust update for stiff collisions, so its stated second-order low-rank IMEX construction and stiff-regime robustness are unsupported in general.
issues.title: Implicit collision update in the backward S-steps can be singular
issues.why_classification: Avoiding the pole while retaining second-order accuracy and stiff robustness requires redesigning a central part of the second-order integrator; simply excluding exact resonance does not control the arbitrarily large amplification nearby.

issues.failure_explanation: Grouping the actual stencil by spatial weights gives the $\beta$-operator $\Delta v^{-2}(\alpha_{q+1/2}w_{q+1}-\alpha_{q-1/2}w_q)$ and the $\beta^{-1}$-operator $\Delta v^{-2}(\alpha_{q-1/2}^{-1}w_{q-1}-\alpha_{q+1/2}^{-1}w_q)$. These are not the two second-difference operators defined in the proof. Moreover, the displayed second-difference operator generally has a $4\alpha_{\max}/\Delta v^2$-type norm bound, not the asserted factor 2. Consequently the proof does not establish the proposition from the given stencil.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the two velocity operators by the correct bidiagonal operators obtained by grouping the stencil, and prove their induced-norm bounds with the stated constants and boundary treatment.
issues.overall_effect: The projection bound and hence the use of its constant $\kappa_h$ in the main relaxation theorem are unsupported as written.
issues.title: The operator decomposition used in the fluctuation projection proof is not the stated stencil
issues.why_classification: The actual stencil admits the intended two-term spatial decomposition, and a short local correction of the velocity operators and norm estimate appears sufficient without changing the proposition's substantive bound.

issues.failure_explanation: A maximum over geometric half-grid values need not bound the nodal values multiplying $\rho$ and $g/M$. For example, when the Gaussian Maxwellian is maximal at a velocity node, both adjacent geometric means are strictly smaller than that nodal maximum. The two norm inequalities used to absorb the fluctuation therefore do not follow from the theorem's definition of $M_{\max}^{n+1}$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define a separate maximum over nodal values $M_{p,q}^{n+1}$ and use it consistently in the state, fluctuation, absorption, and final estimates, retaining half-grid extrema only where the dissipation argument requires them.
issues.overall_effect: The constants, small-fluctuation condition, and both bounds in the theorem are unjustified with the stated half-grid maximum.
issues.title: The main theorem uses a half-grid maximum to bound nodal Maxwellian values
issues.why_classification: This is a local correction of the constants and associated hypothesis; it does not require a new argument or alter the qualitative $\mathcal O(\varepsilon+\kappa_h)$ estimate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where \(\rho(x,t)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_v}}f\,\dv\) is the charge density and $\eta(x)$ is a given background charge satisfying the global neutrality condition \(\int_{\Omega_x}(\rho(x,0)-\eta(x))\,\dx=0\).

issues.failure_explanation: On the full velocity line, the two Gaussian terms integrate to $\sqrt{2\pi}$ and $\sqrt{2\pi T_{\rm cold}}$, respectively. Hence the velocity integral of the displayed $f^0$ is $\rho^0(x)(1+\sqrt{T_{\rm cold}})$, not $\rho^0(x)$; truncation to $[-6,6]$ does not restore equality. Thus the declared density and the background chosen for it are inconsistent with the distribution used in the Poisson equation and neutrality condition.

failure_location.quote:
with spatially localized density and background charge
\[
  \rho^0(x)=0.3+\exp\!\Big(-\frac{(x-0.3)^2}{0.01}\Big),\qquad
  \eta(x)=0.3+\exp\!\Big(-\frac{(x-0.6)^2}{0.01}\Big),
\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Normalize the cold Gaussian and specify its intended mass fraction, or redefine the actual density and adjust the background charge to enforce neutrality; then recompute the benchmark.
issues.overall_effect: The bump-on-tail benchmark is not a self-consistent VPFP initial-value problem as specified, so its electric field and all numerical comparisons for that test are ambiguous.
issues.title: The bump-on-tail distribution does not have the declared density
issues.why_classification: Several mathematically distinct normalizations are possible, and any consistent choice changes the initial charge and field and requires rerunning the numerical experiment, although the defect is confined to one benchmark.
